sentences.text: Unasuchus is an extinct genus of eusuchian crocodyliforms belonging to the family Hylaeochampsidae, known only from skull and jaw fragments.
The genus name Unasuchus honors the municipality of Uña in central Spain, where the fossils were discovered. The type species, Unasuchus reginae, was formally named in 1992.
Cladistic analysis suggests that Unasuchus is a derived member of the family Hylaeochampsidae.

Unasuchus lived during the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous, with fossils found in the Barremian Las Hoyas Formation. The genus existed from the Hauterivian to the Barremian, between 132.6 and 121.4 million years ago.
